docs.text:
This site is a collection of simple, practical systems designed to make everyday life easier to manage.

The goal is not complexity, but clarity—clear steps, clear structure, and repeatable processes that remove guesswork from important areas like money, work, and personal growth.

Core Areas Money System — Manage income, savings, and taxes with structure Technology — Build and understand real-world systems Personal Systems — Stay consistent and focused How to Use This

Start with one system, follow it step-by-step, and build consistency over time. Each section is designed to stand on its own but work together as part of a larger framework.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this laboratory you will be able to

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text:
Open: ~/.config/starship/starship.toml

Replace its contents with: 

add_newline = false
command_timeout = 1000

format = """
$os\
$username\
$hostname\
$python\
$docker_context\
$kubernetes\
$directory\
$git_branch\
$git_status\
$cmd_duration
"""

[character]
success_symbol = ""
error_symbol = ""

[os]
disabled = false
format = "[$symbol](bold white) "

[os.symbols]
Ubuntu = " "
Windows = " "
Arch = " "
Macos = " "

[username]
show_always = true
format = "[$user](bold white) "

[hostname]
ssh_only = false
format = "on [$hostname](bold yellow) "

[directory]
truncation_length = 2
home_symbol = "~"
format = "at [$path]($style) "

[git_branch]
symbol = " "
format = "via [$symbol$branch]($style) "

[git_status]
format = "[$all_status$ahead_behind]($style)"

[python]
disabled = false
symbol = "🐍 "
format = "via [$symbol$virtualenv]($style) "

[docker_context]
disabled = false
symbol = "🐳 "
format = "via [$symbol$context]($style) "

[kubernetes]
disabled = false
symbol = "☸ "
format = "on [$symbol$context($namespace)]($style) "

[cmd_duration]
min_time = 500
format = "took [$duration](bold yellow) "
This preserves my personal Starship prompt while also adding effects for Python, Docker, Kubernetes, & command timing.

It is built on real-world use—simple enough to follow consistently, but structured enough to prevent common financial mistakes. The focus is on control, not restriction; on understanding, not guesswork.

Managing money doesn’t have to be complicated, but it does require structure. Most financial stress comes from not knowing where money is going or what it needs to do next.

This system is designed to remove that uncertainty. By giving every dollar a clear purpose from the moment it’s received, you create a simple, repeatable process that keeps you in control.

The goal isn’t perfection—it’s consistency. Small, disciplined actions taken over time lead to stability, confidence, and long-term growth.

docs.title: The 4-account money system
docs.text:
The 4-account money system is a simple way to manage income by separating it into clear, purpose-driven categories. Instead of keeping all money in one place, each dollar is assigned a job as soon as it comes in.

The system consists of four core accounts:

Spending (Checking): Used for everyday expenses like bills, food, and personal purchases. Taxes (High-Yield Savings): A dedicated account where a percentage of income (typically 25–30%) is set aside to cover future tax obligations. Savings (Emergency Fund): Reserved for unexpected expenses such as car repairs, medical costs, or temporary loss of income. Investing (Wealth Building): Long-term funds placed into accounts like a Roth IRA or brokerage account to grow over time.

By splitting income immediately upon receiving it, this system removes guesswork, prevents overspending, and ensures that taxes, emergencies, and future growth are consistently accounted for. It creates structure, discipline, and financial clarity without requiring complex budgeting.

docs.title: Using the System to Pay Taxes Efficiently
docs.text:
One of the biggest advantages of the 4-account system is how it simplifies paying taxes. By consistently setting aside a percentage of income (typically 25–30%) into a dedicated tax account, you avoid the stress of scrambling for money at the end of the year.

When this tax account is a high-yield savings account, it does more than just hold money—it earns interest over time. As your income is deposited and your tax portion is set aside, the balance gradually grows. The bank pays you interest for holding that money, effectively generating a small return on funds that you would have owed anyway.

By the end of the year, you have:

The full amount needed to pay your taxes Additional money earned from interest

This means your tax obligation is fully covered, and the interest earned either offsets part of the tax burden or becomes extra money you keep. Instead of taxes feeling like a sudden loss, the system turns it into a controlled, predictable process that even works slightly in your favor.

The key is consistency—setting aside money immediately when income is received and leaving it untouched until taxes are due.

  2. Let the money sit:
    • Earn interest over time
    • Do not touch it
  3. When taxes are due:
    • Pay directly from the tax account

Check Valves

Confirm the following:

  • Suction valves are OPEN.
  • Multiport valve is set to FILTER.
  • Air relief valve is closed (unless priming the system).

docs.title: Step 3 — Prime the Pump
docs.text:
Remove Air From the System

If the pump has lost prime:

  1. Fill the pump basket with water.
  2. Open the air relief valve.
  3. Allow trapped air to escape.
  4. Close the valve once water flows steadily.
  5. Ensure the pump basket is completely full before continuing.

docs.title: Step 4 — Start the Pump
docs.text:
Begin Water Circulation

Turn the pump ON.

Verify:

  • Water begins circulating.
  • Pump sounds smooth and normal.
  • No excessive air bubbles are visible.
  • No leaks appear around hoses or fittings.

docs.title: Step 5 — Verify Sand Filter Operation
docs.text:
Check the Filter

Confirm:

  • Strong return flow into the pool.
  • No water leaking around fittings.
  • Filter pressure appears normal.
  • Water is circulating continuously.

docs.title: Step 6 — Enable the QS1200 Saltwater System
docs.text:
Start Chlorine Generation

After normal water circulation has been established:

  • Turn ON the QS1200.
  • Verify normal indicator lights.
  • Confirm there are no warning or error lights.
  • Verify water is flowing in the correct direction through the unit.

docs.title: Step 7 — Final Inspection
docs.text:
Startup Complete

Confirm all of the following:

  • ✅ Pump running smoothly
  • ✅ Strong return flow
  • ✅ No water leaks
  • ✅ No trapped air
  • ✅ QS1200 operating normally
  • ✅ Pool ready for normal operation

docs.title: Common Startup Problems
docs.text:
💧 Pump runs, but no water is moving

Check these items in order:

  • Verify pool water level.
  • Ensure both suction valves are open.
  • Prime the pump again.
  • Check hoses for kinks.
  • Inspect intake screens for blockages.
🔊 Pump is noisy

Common causes:

  • Air trapped in the plumbing.
  • Low water level.
  • Loose suction-side fitting.
  • Pump not fully primed.
🌊 Weak or No Return Flow

Possible causes:

  • Dirty sand filter.
  • Pump not primed.
  • Closed valve.
  • Blocked hose.
  • Dirty skimmer basket.
🧂 QS1200 Will Not Start

Verify:

  • Pump is circulating water.
  • Salt level is within specification.
  • Power is connected.
  • Water is flowing in the correct direction.
  • No warning lights are displayed.

docs.title: ⏱️ Expected Startup Timeline
docs.text:
Normal Startup Timing

Approximate startup times:

Pump starts: Immediately

Water reaches the return jet: 30–60 seconds

Air clears from the system: 1–2 minutes

QS1200: Turn ON only after steady water flow has been established.

docs.title: 💡 Startup Tips
docs.text:
Helpful Reminders
  • Follow the steps in order.
  • Don't rush the priming process.
  • Listen for unusual pump noises.
  • Watch for leaks during the first few minutes.
  • If something doesn't look right, stop and inspect before continuing.
  • Most startup issues are caused by trapped air, low water level, or closed valves.

docs.title: 🚀 Startup Complete
docs.text:
Once all checks have passed, the system should be operating normally.

If a problem develops after startup:

  • 🗺️ Review the System Diagram
  • ⚠️ Open the Troubleshooting guide
  • 🧹 Continue to Maintenance
  • 📦 Check the Parts Reference

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
🕐 Five Minute Rule

Spend five minutes checking the simple things first.

  • Is there power?
  • Is there water?
  • Are the valves open?
  • Are the hoses connected?
  • Is the filter clean?

Most problems are solved here.

flowchart TD

START([Pump won't circulate])

START --> POWER{Pump has power?}

POWER -- No --> BREAKER["Check breaker
Check GFCI
Check timer"]

POWER -- Yes --> PRIME{Pump primed?}

PRIME -- No --> AIR["Open air valve
Fill pump basket
Remove trapped air"]

PRIME -- Yes --> FLOW{Water flowing?}

FLOW -- No --> BLOCKAGE["Inspect:

• Suction hoses
• T-valve
• Skimmer
• Pump basket"]

FLOW -- Yes --> SALT{E.C.O. running?}

SALT -- No --> CHECKFLOW["Verify flow sensor
Verify arrows
Check salt level"]

SALT -- Yes --> GOOD([System Operating Normally])

docs.title: Quick Jump
docs.text:
• 🛑 Pump won't start
  • 💧 Pump runs, but no water moves
  • 🌊 Weak water flow
  • 🧂 Salt system warning
  • 💨 Air bubbles
  • 🔄 Need to backwash
  • 🚫 Things to Never Do
✅ What Normal Looks Like

If everything is working correctly, you should see:

  • Strong water flow from the return jet.
  • Pump running smoothly without unusual noises.
  • No continuous stream of air bubbles.
  • QS1200 operating normally.
  • Water level approximately halfway up the skimmer opening.
🛑 Pump won't start 💧 Pump runs but no water is moving

Follow these steps in order:

  1. Verify the pool water level.
  2. Make sure both suction valves are open.
  3. Open the air relief valve to remove trapped air.
  4. Check for clogged intake screens.
  5. Inspect hoses for kinks.
  6. Verify the pump basket is full of water (primed).

Tip

Most circulation problems are caused by trapped air or low water level.

🌊 Water flow is weak

Possible causes:

  • Dirty sand filter
  • Full pump basket
  • Low water level
  • Air leak on suction side
  • Clogged intake
🧂 QS1200 Salt System isn't producing chlorine

Verify:

  • Pump is running.
  • Water is flowing normally.
  • Salt level is within specification.
  • Cell is clean.
  • Water is flowing in the correct direction through the unit.

Info

The QS1200 should always be installed after the sand filter.

🔄 Need to Backwash?

Perform a backwash if:

  • Water flow has noticeably decreased.
  • Filter pressure has increased.
  • Water appears dirty after normal operation.
💨 Air bubbles coming back into the pool

Small bubbles during startup are normal.

Constant bubbles usually indicate:

  • Loose hose clamp
  • Loose pump lid
  • Cracked hose
  • Air leak on the suction side

Tip

Air leaks happen before the pump.

Water leaks usually happen after the pump.

That's a quick way to narrow down where to look.

🚫 Never Do These
  • Never run the pump without water.
  • Never run the QS1200 without water flow.
  • Never change the multiport valve while the pump is running.
  • Never operate with closed suction valves.
  • Never disconnect hoses while the system is pressurized.
❓Still Not Working?

Follow this order:

  1. Stop the pump.
  2. Open the System Diagram page.
  3. Verify every hose follows the arrows.
  4. Check every valve position.
  5. Restart using the Startup page.
  6. If it still doesn't work, begin troubleshooting again from the top.

Success

Don't skip around.

Start at the beginning and work one step at a time.

docs.title: Check these first
docs.text:
• GFCI outlet has not tripped.
  • Circuit breaker is ON.
  • Timer (if installed) is ON.
  • Power cord is securely plugged in.
  • Reset button has been pressed.

Motor hums but won't spin

Turn the pump OFF immediately.

Continuing to run the pump can damage the motor.

docs.title: Recommended Action
docs.text:
Start with the easiest checks:

  1. Empty the basket.
  2. Check the water level.
  3. Backwash the filter if needed.

docs.title: Backwash Procedure
docs.text:
1. Turn pump OFF.
  2. Rotate valve to BACKWASH.
  3. Run for about 2 minutes.
  4. Turn OFF.
  5. Rotate to RINSE.
  6. Run for 30 seconds.
  7. Return valve to FILTER.
  8. Restart pump.
